RagShortTexts: Larger payments can use weighed silver and local ingots.
Weight, fineness and form require checking.

Variants.Content: Grivna and other weighed silver serve larger payments. Parties inspect weight, fineness and regional forms. Acceptance settles the obligation; division, reweighing and change add work, while smaller daily exchanges need separate arrangements.
Soldiers receiving silver need its accounting weight and local acceptance. Witnessed weighing prevents disputes only discovered when buying food elsewhere.
Collectors specify the scale for the transaction and check fineness. Named receivers and accounts reduce conflicting claims of short payment after silver changes hands.
Weighing delays bargains but limits disputes over quality and shortage. A household holding an ingot still needs someone willing to accept or divide it for food.
